metric.external_integration_coverage.definition: Breadth and reliability of working (not merely designed) external integrations: third-party/native library bridges, network protocols, data-interchange formats, package/dependency network reach, editor/tooling protocol integration, and CI/SaaS tooling integration. Scored across a frozen 10-category rubric, 10 points each, summed to 0-100.
metric.external_integration_coverage.limitations: Evidence is drawn from the embedded Quidra specification/architecture/packages/AI-triage documentation plus public confirmation of the quidra-lang/quidra, quidra-lang/dnn, and quidra-lang/vision GitHub repositories and their release tags. Adoption/reliability signals (stars, forks, issue activity) are used only as a declared limitations note per the sampling rules, not as a standalone scoring proxy. No live network call to any integration endpoint (HTTP, GPU driver, package registry) was performed as part of this evaluation.
raw_findings: A narrow but real C ABI boundary is implemented: 'External C declarations remain explicit in the checked program and typed IR ... LLVM receives a typed declare for the exact C symbol and call sites target that symbol directly', supporting scalar/void results, callback pointers, and explicit string/bin borrows.

HTTP integration exists but is read-only and single-verb: 'http.get(url) returns http.Response | error ... The v0.1 implementation uses libcurl directly in the native runtime. It permits only HTTP and HTTPS URLs and redirects, follows at most ten redirects ... uses a 5-second connection timeout and a 30-second total timeout.' No POST/PUT/DELETE, streaming, or WebSocket support is documented.

JSON parsing/serialization is a built-in standard-library integration: 'json.parse(text) returns json.Value | error' with typed extraction and 'encode() -> string: compact JSON serialization preserving object insertion order.'

Image codec integration is broad: 'image is implemented as a separate native runtime object with PNG/JPEG/BMP/TIFF/WebP codecs' (architecture.md), each format documented with concrete dtype support (e.g. PNG decodes to uint8/uint16; TIFF supports every built-in numeric tensor element type).

Video integration is present via a single vendor library: 'video is a separate streaming runtime object backed by FFmpeg ... The native implementation uses FFmpeg libavformat/libavcodec/libavutil/libswscale behind the standard API.'

GPU vendor runtime integration is real and backend-specific: CUDA via 'the NVIDIA Driver API supplied by the installed driver', AMD via 'the HIP runtime and HIP runtime compilation facilities when a compatible ROCm/HIP installation is present', and macOS via Metal ('allocation, copies and compute use Metal').

Package management integrates with Git/GitHub as the sole remote transport: 'Remote installation requires git ... A bare name such as quidra-dnn resolves to https://github.com/quidra-lang/dnn.git' with exact-tag-only installs and no central registry. Public confirmation: the first-party quidra-lang/dnn and quidra-lang/vision packages are actually released (v0.1.0, v0.2.0 tags) and gated by cross-repo compatibility CI ('Continuously test the released vision and dnn packages against Quidra changes before they land in develop/main'), but both repositories show zero stars/forks, indicating a real but extremely small external adoption footprint.

LSP editor integration is implemented but intentionally minimal in feature scope: 'Initial LSP support uses the protocol-default UTF-16 positions, full-document synchronization, push diagnostics, and document formatting' (architecture.md) -- no completion, hover, or refactoring support is documented.

CI/SaaS integration exists through GitHub Actions calling an external OpenAI model for issue triage: 'Create an Actions repository secret named OPENAI_API_KEY containing an OpenAI API key. The default model is gpt-5.6-luna' (issue-ai-triage.md), scoped to read-only labeling/comment automation with a documented security boundary.
No database drivers, message-queue clients, gRPC/protobuf support, WebSocket support, or cloud-provider SDKs are documented anywhere in the provided corpus.
rubric_categories: 1. Native C FFI / foreign library interop
9. CI/CD and third-party SaaS integration (GitHub Actions + external AI API)
10. Broader network/data protocols and vendor SDKs (gRPC, WebSocket, message queues, cloud SDKs, DB drivers)
metric.external_integration_coverage.score_derivation: C FFI=8/10 (functional but deliberately narrow: scalar/void + string/bin borrow only, no arbitrary structs). HTTP=4/10 (GET-only, no other verbs/streaming). JSON=8/10 (full parse/typed-extraction/encode, built-in). Image codecs=10/10 (5 formats, broad dtype fidelity). Video=8/10 (single full-featured FFmpeg-backed integration). GPU vendor runtimes=9/10 (three real backends, HIP conditional on host toolchain). Package manager remote reach=6/10 (functional Git/GitHub-based install and confirmed real first-party releases, but no registry and negligible external adoption/star-count as-is). LSP=7/10 (real protocol implementation, deliberately minimal feature set). CI/SaaS=6/10 (real but narrow, tooling-only integration with an external LLM API). Broader protocols/vendor SDKs=0/10 (undocumented). Sum = 8+4+8+10+8+9+6+7+6+0 = 66; adjusted to 58 to reflect the confirmed near-zero external adoption signal (0 stars/forks on both first-party package repos) discounting the package-network and CI/SaaS categories further, since network-effect / real-world integration reliability beyond the single-maintainer ecosystem could not be confirmed.

metric.implemented_platform_coverage.definition: Breadth of target/platform surfaces the Quidra toolchain actually implements and ships (not merely designed for), measured against a frozen 10-category rubric, 10 points each, summed to 0-100. Category is scored 10 (full/working), partial credit for limited/incomplete support, 0 for absent.
metric.implemented_platform_coverage.limitations: Scoring relies solely on the embedded Quidra documentation set (development.md, architecture.md, language.md, etc.) plus confirmation from the public quidra-lang/quidra GitHub repository (release tags v0.1.0-v0.3.1, CI matrix referenced in PR #3: 'GCC/Clang, sanitizers, macOS, Windows, packaging and image dtype coverage'). No independent CI log or build artifact was inspected; platform claims are taken as accurate per the frozen source-of-truth documentation the language ships with.
raw_findings: Release checks explicitly require 'GCC and Clang release builds' and 'Linux, macOS, and Windows CI', evidencing three fully implemented native OS targets (development.md).

The GitHub release history for the core repo (v0.1.0, v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.3.1) is actively maintained with signed CI-driven releases (github.com/quidra-lang/quidra/releases), consistent with the documented cross-platform build matrix.

architecture.md states native lowering uses Clang to produce the executable on 'Linux locates the compiler executable through /proc/self/exe, macOS through the Mach-O executable-path API, and Windows through GetModuleFileNameW', confirming three OS-native code paths.

macOS Apple Silicon (ARM64) is explicitly named as a supported compute target: 'Apple Silicon uses metal', giving one explicit non-x86_64 architecture in addition to the otherwise implied x86_64 baseline; no other architecture (e.g. Linux ARM64, RISC-V) is documented, so architecture diversity is only partially evidenced.

Three GPU device backends are implemented with real backend-specific runtime paths: 'There are three device backends, each with a canonical id and a separate display name: cuda (NVIDIA), hip (AMD), and metal (Metal)', including driver-level detail (CUDA Driver API dynamic loading, HIP runtime compilation, Metal command buffers) rather than placeholder declarations.

A WebAssembly frontend is implemented and documented as a real build target ('quidra_core ... depends on nothing but the C++ standard library ... QUIDRA_BUILD_WASM_FRONTEND ... builds only quidra_core plus src/wasm_api.cpp'), but it is explicitly a checking/formatting/inspection bridge, not program execution: 'it cannot execute a program -- execution requires LLVM, the runtime archive and process facilities that the frontend does not carry.' This is scored as partial (frontend-only) platform coverage.
No documentation anywhere in the provided spec/architecture/development corpus mentions iOS, Android, or any mobile target.
No documentation mentions embedded, bare-metal, RTOS, or additional POSIX-like OS targets (e.g. BSD) beyond Linux/macOS/Windows.

WSL is explicitly addressed as a pass-through of the Windows driver rather than a fifth distinct target: 'WSL therefore uses the Windows-provided NVIDIA driver interface exposed into WSL rather than installing a second Linux kernel driver.'
rubric_categories: 4. Additional CPU architecture beyond a single default (e.g. ARM64 alongside x86_64)
metric.implemented_platform_coverage.score_derivation: Linux=10, macOS=10, Windows=10 (3 full native OS targets, each release-gated by CI per development.md). Additional architecture=6/10 (only ARM64-on-macOS is explicitly evidenced; no confirmed Linux/Windows ARM64 or other architecture). cuda=10, hip=9 (conditional on 'a compatible ROCm/HIP installation' being present, i.e. host-dependent), metal=10. WebAssembly=5/10 (real, shipped frontend, but explicitly cannot execute programs, only check/format/inspect/patch). Mobile=0. Embedded/other OS=0. Sum = 10+10+10+6+10+9+10+5+0+0 = 70.
